title: Scheme-test open-subset identities through a fixed etale atlas
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. All schemes are over $S$ in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $|E|$ for its field-valued point classes and $|t|:|T|\to|E|$ for the map of a scheme-source morphism, as in [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Fix a representable surjective etale morphism $w:h_W\to E$ from a scheme, and let $t:h_T\to E$ be any morphism from a scheme. The sheaf fibre product $Q=T\times_EW$ is represented by a scheme. Write $q:Q\to T$ and $b:Q\to W$ for its projections. The map $q$ is surjective etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence continuous and open on scheme points. For every subset $A\subseteq|E|$, $$ |q|^{-1}(|t|^{-1}(A))=|b|^{-1}(|w|^{-1}(A)),\qquad |q|\bigl(|b|^{-1}(|w|^{-1}(A))\bigr)=|t|^{-1}(A). $$ If $|w|^{-1}(A)$ is open, then $|t|^{-1}(A)$ is open. For every subset $B\subseteq|T|$, $$ |b|\bigl(|q|^{-1}(B)\bigr)=|w|^{-1}(|t|(B)). $$ If $t$ is representable etale and $B$ is open in $T$, then $b$ is etale and the last displayed subset is open in $W$. These assertions use only the scheme topologies and assume no topology on $|E|$.

proof.text: Use [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] to choose the representing scheme Q and its projections q,b, retaining its explicit common-field point-lifting property. Apply the scheme-test predicates [def-trf-algebraic-space] for w to obtain etale and surjective representing squares. Yoneda full faithfulness and uniqueness of the representing pullback identify each of these squares with Q, so q is etale and surjective. Scheme morphisms are continuous [def-pc-scheme], and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] makes q open.

proof.text: The pullback square satisfies $t\circ h_q=w\circ h_b$. For $z\in Q$, the residue-field maps $\kappa(q(z))\to\kappa(z)$ and $\kappa(b(z))\to\kappa(z)$ show that the classes defining $|t|(|q|(z))$ and $|w|(|b|(z))$ have equal representatives over $\kappa(z)$, by that square. Thus $|t|\circ|q|=|w|\circ|b|$ by [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes].

source.place: Tag 03BX (lemma-topology-points), proof: the presentation pullback diagram and scheme-topological openness; Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), common-field lifting of compatible points.

proof.text: For $A\subseteq|E|$, membership in either $|q|^{-1}(|t|^{-1}(A))$ or $|b|^{-1}(|w|^{-1}(A))$ means that the common value in step 2 belongs to $A$, proving the first equality. Since $|q|$ is surjective, every $x\in|t|^{-1}(A)$ has a lift $z\in Q$; the first equality places $z$ in $|b|^{-1}(|w|^{-1}(A))$. Conversely the image of that subset under $|q|$ lies in $|t|^{-1}(A)$. This proves the second equality.

source.place: Tag 03BX (lemma-topology-points), proof: the presentation pullback diagram and scheme-topological openness; Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), common-field lifting of compatible points.

proof.text: If $|w|^{-1}(A)$ is open in $W$, its inverse image under the continuous $|b|$ is open in $Q$. Its image under the open map $|q|$ is open in $T$, and step 3 identifies that image with $|t|^{-1}(A)$.

proof.text: First bridge quotient equality to the explicit common-field witnesses accepted by [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point]. The relation defining [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes] is reflexive and symmetric. For transitivity, form the fibre product of the two common field spectra over the middle representative [def-pc-fibre-product]. Their unique points have the same image. By the Mathlib leaf [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-pullback-compatible-point], this fibre product has a point; its residue field supplies a common extension. Functoriality of the presheaf maps proves the transitive relation. Therefore equality in the generated quotient implies one common-field relation. For residue-field representatives of x,y, compose its two maps with the residue-field maps to T,W; these have the required underlying points. Now for B in T, commutativity gives b(q-inverse(B)) contained in w-inverse(t(B)). Conversely choose x in B with t(x)=w(y), use the quotient bridge and the point-lifting clause of [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] to find z with q(z)=x and b(z)=y. This proves the image equality.

source.place: Tag 03BX (lemma-topology-points), proof: the presentation pullback diagram and scheme-topological openness; Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), common-field lifting of compatible points.

proof.text: If $t$ is representable etale, its scheme test along $w$ says that $b:Q\to W$ is etale [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For open $B\subseteq|T|$, the set $|q|^{-1}(B)$ is open by continuity of $|q|$, and its image under $|b|$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. Step 5 identifies this image with $|w|^{-1}(|t|(B))$. Every openness assertion concerned only the scheme spaces $Q,T,W$; no topology on $|E|$ was used.
